0|fa5e084e43eb14c14942027e1e2e894aeed96097|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"vmscan: do not unconditionally treat zones that fail zone_reclaim() as full
On NUMA machines
column2: the administrator can configure zone_reclaim_mode that

column1: is a more targetted form of direct reclaim.  On machines with large NUMA
distances for example
column2: a zone_reclaim_mode defaults to 1 meaning that

column1: clean unmapped pages will be reclaimed if the zone watermarks are not
being met.  The problem is that zone_reclaim() failing at all means the
zone gets marked full.
This can cause situations where a zone is usable
because it has been considered full.  Take a situation where a large tmpfs
mount is occuping a large percentage of memory overall.  The pages do not
get cleaned or reclaimed by zone_reclaim()
column2: but the zone gets marked full

column1: and the zonelist cache considers them not worth trying in the future.
This patch makes zone_reclaim() return more fine-grained information about
what occured when zone_reclaim() failued.  The zone only gets marked full
if it really is unreclaimable.  If it's a case that the scan did not occur
or if enough pages were not reclaimed with the limited reclaim_mode
the zone is simply skipped.
There is a side-effect to this patch.  Currently
successfully reclaimed SWAP_CLUSTER_MAX
ahead.  With this patch applied
zone_reclaim() does some work.
This bug was introduced by commit 9276b1bc96a132f4068fdee00983c532f43d3a26
(""memory page_alloc zonelist caching speedup"") way back in 2.6.19 when the
zonelist_cache was introduced.  It was not intended that zone_reclaim()
aggressively consider the zone to be full when it failed as full direct
reclaim can still be an option.  Due to the age of the bug
considered a -stable candidate.
